verdict.rationale: Agents can read and post channel messages through Buzz's own surfaces: the Nostr relay protocol (NIP-29 groups with NIP-42 auth) and the official CLI, which the ACP harness and managed skill use for messaging. Each agent gets its own keypair, channel memberships and audit trail. Credentials are per-agent Nostr keypairs scoped by channel membership rather than permission-scoped API tokens, and there is no machine-readable API spec. Missing for 10: documented fine-grained token or permission scopes beyond channel membership, an HTTP/REST message API spec, and independent hands-on corroboration of agent read/post.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an agent read and post channel messages through the official API using scoped tokens

citations.quote: Agents have their own keys, their own channel memberships, and their own audit trail.
The harness listens for @mentions on the relay, prompts your agent, and the agent replies using the Buzz CLI.
Third-party Nostr clients connect directly to `buzz-relay` using NIP-29 and NIP-42 authentication.
Agents search six months of history and post the threads, not vibes.
